_comment: Pre-registered council ATTENDANCE metrics (road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b Phase 1.4). Registered here rather than in roadmap prose because a roadmap is archived when it closes and a metric outlives it — the sibling budget files (hook-token-budget.json, recycle-threshold-budget.json) already carry the owner / review_by / honest-gap discipline this reuses. The instrument is the quorum_result line appendQuorumEvent writes to agents/runtime/council/events.log (schema v2); nothing here is measured yet, and no threshold is committed before data exists.
privacy: a quorum_result line carries {phase, command, dispatch, verdict, threshold, configured_total, total, present, solo, absent[{member, reason}]} — counts, closed vocabularies, and member ids only. The type has no field able to hold free-form content, so the CLI's own `detail` string (provider error text, which can embed paths and prompt fragments) is dropped at the boundary rather than scrubbed.
phase_split: A pass emits `pre_run` (build_members — who could be constructed) and, on the `run` path, `post_run` (_postRunQuorum — who actually returned a usable response). They disagree whenever a member constructs and then fails mid-flight, so a rate computed over both double-counts. A `pre_run` line is NOT evidence a pass ran: `command: estimate` is a spend-free preview, and a `run` / `debate` line is written before the `--confirm` gate (which defaults to false and returns before any provider call) and before the necessity and size-fit gates. A `post_run` line is the only line that proves providers were called — which is why every rate below is post_run-scoped, and why `command` exists at all.

attendance_rate.definition: of the members that entered the pass, how many answered: present / total per post_run pass. Bounded by 1 by construction (evaluateQuorum clamps present into [0, total]).
attendance_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, fields present + total
attendance_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date

roster_shortfall_rate.definition: how often the council shrank BEFORE the pass: share of post_run passes with total < configured_total, plus the size of the gap. This is the half attendance_rate cannot see — a pass with 3 configured, 2 failing to construct and 1 answering reads 1/1 = 100 % attendance and a shortfall of 2. Both numbers are needed and neither substitutes for the other; a single ratio over mixed rosters is the error this pair replaces.
roster_shortfall_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, configured_total vs total
roster_shortfall_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date
roster_shortfall_rate.not_an_error: total > configured_total is legitimate and not a shortfall: `--siblings` fans ONE enabled config entry into N clients, so the client roster can exceed the entry count. configured_total counts enabled config ENTRIES; total counts CLIENTS. Compare them for direction, never divide one by the other.

solo_conclusion_rate.definition: share of post_run passes with `solo: true` — written by the isSoloConcluded predicate in quorum.ts, never re-derived from the numbers here, so one change to the rule cannot leave this definition stale. ceil(n/2) makes 1-of-2 a legitimate conclusion; this measures how often that legitimacy is used, not whether it should be. THREE cases carry solo: true and they are not the same finding — a degraded multi-member council (configured_total > 1), a council configured with one member (configured_total = 1, dispatch = full), and a deliberate --single dispatch (dispatch = single). Split on dispatch and configured_total before reading the rate.
solo_conclusion_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field solo, split by dispatch + configured_total
solo_conclusion_rate.threshold: DECIDED 2026-08-11 against real data — see ADR-224 (docs/decisions/ADR-224-gate-scoped-solo-attendance-floor.md). The quorum-solo-floor blocker pre-registered three outcomes — a third CLI member, a gate-scoped min_present: 2, or a published null under 5 %. Read at 2026-08-11T09:30Z with the definition above: 1 of 8 post_run/command=run passes carried a degraded solo conclusion = 12.5 %, so the under-5 % null did not fire and the gate-scoped floor was chosen (council 2/2). It was decided on the degraded case only; a --single pass is the operator asking for one voice, not the council failing to assemble. Still no numeric threshold is committed here, deliberately: at n=8 the 95 % interval around 1/8 spans roughly 0.3 %-53 %, so the rate established urgency and not certainty, and ADR-224's review trigger reopens the null at n=40. What this metric measures does NOT change; once the floor lands, how often it FIRES is a second and different question needing its own instrument. THAT INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS — `floor_fire_rate` below, registered 2026-08-11 with the floor itself. Read the two together: a floor-held pass resolves `inconclusive`, so its `solo` field is `false` and THIS rate falls as the floor fires. A post-floor solo rate below 12.5 % is therefore NOT evidence the degradation stopped; no threshold here was loosened, and none was set.

floor_fire_rate.definition: share of post_run passes carrying `held_by_floor: true` — the gate-class attendance floor ADR-224 authorized held a pass whose threshold WAS met. Written by evaluateQuorum, never re-derived: `verdict: 'inconclusive'` alone cannot separate a floor hold from a threshold never reached, which is the single distinction this metric exists to make. Read the denominator as post_run/command=run passes that DECLARED themselves gate-class, not all passes — a pass that supplied no floor cannot fire one, and counting it dilutes the rate toward zero by construction.
floor_fire_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field held_by_floor (schema v3+); the gate-class subset is exactly the lines that can carry `true`
floor_fire_rate.threshold: none committed before data — deliberately, and for the same reason solo_conclusion_rate committed none: the decision that authorized this floor was made at n=8 with a 95 % interval of roughly 0.3 %-53 %. A threshold set now would be set on that same thin sample. Baseline first; ADR-224's review trigger (2026-11-10, or n=40 post_run/command=run passes) is where a number becomes defensible.
floor_fire_rate.why_this_is_not_a_duplicate_of_solo_conc: They are successor instruments measuring opposite sides of one event. A floor-held pass resolves `inconclusive`, so isSoloConcluded returns false and its `solo` field is FALSE — meaning solo_conclusion_rate DEFLATES exactly as this rate rises. Reading either alone after the floor starts firing produces the wrong conclusion: a falling solo rate is not evidence the underlying degradation stopped, only that the floor is catching it. Sum them before comparing against the pre-floor 12.5 % baseline.
floor_fire_rate.expected_value_today: ZERO, and not because the degradation stopped. As of 2026-08-11 no caller in this repository declares a pass gate-class (see the honest gap below), so no pass can carry `held_by_floor: true`. A zero reading is therefore a measurement of the wiring, not of council attendance, until the first consumer lands. Do not report it as a null.

absent_reason_distribution.definition: count per reason over absent[] entries — no_binary / no_auth / timeout / quota (AbsentReason) plus the two runtime fallbacks the CLI writes directly, `unavailable` (transport resolved to nothing) and `binary_missing` (a CLI client refused to construct). Distinguishes a council degraded by configuration from one degraded by provider behaviour, which have opposite fixes.
absent_reason_distribution.instrument: quorum_result lines, absent[].reason, split by phase (a pre_run absence is configuration; a post_run absence is mid-flight). Excluding `command: estimate` is NOT sufficient: `run` and `debate` also reach construction and return at the `--confirm` gate, which defaults to false. The reliable filter is a pre_run line whose pass produced a matching post_run line; a pre_run line with no post_run partner reached construction and stopped there, whatever its command says.
absent_reason_distribution.threshold: none committed before data — the distribution IS the finding at review date
absent_reason_distribution.merge_before_reading: `no_binary` and `binary_missing` are two spellings of one condition — the CLI binary is unusable — written by different code paths (transport_resolver's static classification vs the CLI client's construction failure). They are recorded separately because that is what the tree emits, not because they are separate findings; merge them before reading the distribution, or the largest bucket is split in two.

honest_null_consequence: If the log accumulates and the solo-conclusion rate sits near zero, that is the published answer to the quorum-solo-floor blocker and 1.5 is cancelled against it — not quietly dropped. If attendance data never accumulates at all (nobody runs a metered council pass in the window), that is reported as an unmeasured metric at the review date, never as a passing one.
honest_gaps: `lens` and `invocation` are empty on every pre_run line — neither is known at member-construction time — so any per-lens breakdown is post_run-only.

`command: debate` carries the pre_run half ONLY. There is no _postRunQuorum on the debate path, and defining `usable response` for a multi-round debate is a separate question this registration does not answer. So debate contributes to absent_reason_distribution and to nothing else: attendance_rate and solo_conclusion_rate cover the `run` path, and a reader must not read them as covering every metered pass.

A pre_run line proves construction happened, never that a pass followed — the `--confirm` gate (default false), the necessity gate and the size-fit gate all abort afterwards and nothing on the line records it. Any count over pre_run lines is an upper bound; pair it with a post_run line before treating it as a pass.

THE ADR-224 FLOOR SHIPPED WITH ZERO CALLERS, and that is stated here so a zero `floor_fire_rate` is never read as a null. `evaluateQuorum` accepts an `AttendanceFloor` and defaults it to `null`; supplying one IS the gate-class declaration. As of 2026-08-11 no call site in this repository supplies one — both `evaluateQuorum` call sites (`build_members` and `_postRunQuorum`) pass no floor, so behaviour is byte-identical to pre-ADR-224 and the capability is deliberately inert. The nearest candidate consumer, `legal_review_prep.require_council` (default true, whose rule text says a legal work-product is NEVER single-model and FAIL-CLOSED), is a MODEL-CARRIED obligation: the flag appears only in the settings template, its zod schema, one rule file and one skill file, and no code reads it. Wiring it means threading quorum enforcement into skill execution — an architectural change with its own safety surface, deliberately out of scope here. WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS: the first caller that passes `GATE_CLASS_ATTENDANCE_FLOOR`. Until one does, this floor is a capability plus a measurement, not a protection, and the honest report at the review date is 'inert, zero callers' rather than 'zero fires'.

A CI GATE OVER THIS LOG IS NOT POSSIBLE AS THINGS STAND, and it was considered rather than overlooked. `agents/runtime/council/events.log` is gitignored and worktree-LOCAL: two sessions on the same repository legitimately read different counts (measured 2026-08-11 — one worktree read 3 `quorum_result` lines while another read 18 at the same moment). So a workflow asserting anything over this file would be asserting over whatever the runner happens to have, which is nothing on a fresh checkout. Any future alarm on these metrics needs a durable, shared sink first; that is a prerequisite, not a detail.

The CLI emit wiring itself has no test. The two modules are covered directly, but nothing exercises build_members / cmd_run / cmd_debate end-to-end against a captured log — and `_emitQuorumEvent` forwards no AppendEventOptions, so there is no target to capture into. Two defects in this file's first version (a `dispatch` written from the flag rather than the outcome, and a rate mixing config entries with clients) were found by review rather than by a test, which is what that gap costs.
